visual.general_description: Vertical timeline diagram with nine numbered dated entries summarizing the patient's hospital course.
visual.detailed_description: Tall vertical timeline on a white background with a central black line and nine numbered circles alternating left and right, each beside a colored date banner and a text box. 1: 2024/01/02, the patient reported with generalized edema, arterial hypertension, and dyspnea; diagnosed with severe preeclampsia and acute pulmonary edema; admitted for urgent obstetric care. 2: 2024/01/03, an emergency cesarean section was performed due to clinical deterioration; postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony after cesarean section; the patient developed severe hypovolemic shock and was transferred to the ICU. 3: 2024/01/04 to 2024/01/10, ICU stay; diagnosed with HELLP syndrome (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets); managed with blood products and antihypertensives; symptoms included asthenia, dizziness, pallor, and RUQ pain. 4: 2024/01/11 to 2024/01/20, transferred to the hospital ward; reported arthralgia, fatigue, facial erythema, and photosensitivity; dermatology noted phlyctenas (blisters) on the lower limbs; autoimmune etiology is suspected; rheumatology was consulted. 5: 2024/01/18, documented rupture of flictenas (blisters) in the right lower extremity, similar to a lupus-related skin flare. 6: 2024/01/21 to 2024/01/30, rheumatologic evaluation confirmed Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE); ANA and anti-dsDNA positive; low complement levels (C3/C4); massive vulvar edema was observed and resolved with non-invasive method; oral iron was started for persistent anemia. 7: 2024/01/28, pharmacologic therapy initiated: hydroxychloroquine 5 mg/kg daily and enalapril 20 mg daily. 8: 2024/01/31, subdermal contraceptive implant inserted. 9: 2024/02/27, discharged after a 56-day hospital stay; weight 91 lbs; labs and imaging are within normal limits; discharge diagnoses: SLE (new onset), HELLP syndrome (resolved), postpartum hemorrhage, corrected hypovolemic shock, preeclampsia with pulmonary edema, resolved vulvar edema, and moderate anemia; outpatient rheumatology follow-up arranged. No panel letters, patient names or identifiers are visible; the numbering of the circles is printed 1 to 9 but the order of banners follows the vertical line.
